face_model.description: Detector stack. MUST NOT be a model that performs identity recognition — see the licence note.

batch_size.description: Frames per inference call. ~0.25s/frame measured on CPU either way; batching avoids repeating setup.

frame_stride.description: Process every Nth frame. AU dynamics are slow relative to 30fps and the model is expensive; the stride is recorded so the effective rate is never assumed.

signals.description: FACS Action Unit OCCURRENCE probabilities (XGBoost predict_proba), not intensities — the manifest said intensity until 2026-09-22, which the model never produced. reliability_tier is set PER AU from the published per-unit floor, never uniformly — §2.2 measured AU12 at F1 .72-.83 and AU20 at .13-.24 on the same data with the same model, and a uniform confidence across 20+ units would misrepresent both ends.

Whether a face was found in this frame. Emitted as a signal rather than left implicit because §2.2 measured valid-face-frame yield at 43% vs 62-63% between engines on identical video — the denominator is itself a finding.

quality.description: Effective AU sampling rate after frame_stride. Lower than the capture rate by construction, which is why it is measured rather than inferred from the video.
§2.2: 43% (iMotions/AFFDEX) vs 62-63% (FaceReader/Py-Feat) on identical video. This number is engine-specific and must never be compared across engines as if it were a property of the recording.
§2.5: the only quantified bias mitigation in the evidence base.

license.notes: Py-Feat's own code is MIT. BUT its default detector stack can include an InsightFace ArcFace weight that is non-commercial, and ArcFace is an IDENTITY model — it is not needed for AU work and is excluded by this engine's params. Marked `unknown` rather than `yes` deliberately: the AU model's own weight licence was NOT separately confirmed during research, and the licence tool buckets unknown as unverified rather than permissive. Re-verify before any commercial ship.
